references.shows: The low-E-flat YCL-221II has an arching silver neck, long straight keyed body, short upturned silver bell and a floor peg.
Anatomy overview and illustrated instrument variants: Single-reed mouthpiece on curved neck. Long straight dark body with silver keywork.
Photographic reference collection for bass clarinet: compare long straight dark body with silver keywork and metal lower bow ending in an upturned bell. Select the variant described in notes.

silhouette: A long dark woodwind held upright, with a curved metal neck at the top and upturned metal bell below.
features: Long straight dark body with silver keywork
Metal lower bow ending in an upturned bell
iconFeatures: Upright long dark tube with hooked neck and lower bell
avoid: An alto saxophone or straight soprano clarinet
Brand logos, wordmarks and decorative text that obscure the instrument anatomy
notes: The low-E-flat YCL-221II guides the upright playing pose and the compact bell. The artwork simplifies the long key rods and covered keywork.

geometry.proportions: The straight keyed body occupies most of the height. The short bell rises beside the lowest third of the body.
geometry.partLayout: Seat the silver neck in the top joint, arch it toward the player and fit the beaked mouthpiece at its end. Carry the long cylindrical body into the silver U-shaped bell and attach the floor peg below the bow.
